title: Interface-Rooted Repo Maps for Token-Efficient Coding Agents: A Negative Result

contributions.purpose: Reduce token consumption of LLM coding agents via task-focused repository context.
contributions.mechanism: Propose IR-RepoMap, which extracts interface file paths from FeatureBench problem statements, builds a bounded import closure via BFS over the Python import graph, and prepends function/class signatures to the agent prompt.
contributions.evaluation: Presented as a task-conditioned repo map method targeting a hypothesized >=25% token reduction.
contributions.domain: Context efficiency for LLM coding agents
contributions.source_quote: We propose IR-RepoMap, a task-conditioned repository map that leverages interface file paths from FeatureBench problem statements to build focused dependency closures.

contributions.purpose: Empirically test the method under a controlled design.
contributions.mechanism: Evaluate IR-RepoMap on FeatureBench-Lite Level 1 (26 tasks) with OpenHands and DeepSeek-V3, including a random-map null control.
contributions.evaluation: Controlled comparison on 13 comparable tasks against baseline and a random-map control.
contributions.source_quote: We evaluate IR-RepoMap on FeatureBench-Lite Level 1 with a controlled experimental design including a random-map null control.

contributions.mechanism: Measure token consumption of IR-RepoMap versus baseline across tasks.
contributions.evaluation: Negative result: IR-RepoMap uses 20.8% MORE tokens than baseline with extreme per-task variance (std=274.6%, range -89% to +889%).
contributions.source_quote: We report a negative result: static task-conditioned repo maps do not reliably reduce token consumption, with highly task-dependent effects.

contributions.mechanism: Argue from the negative result that dynamic context retrieval outperforms static upfront context provision.
contributions.evaluation: Qualitative recommendation; no separate quantitative evaluation.
contributions.source_quote: We provide insights for future research, suggesting that dynamic context retrieval approaches may be more promising than static upfront provision.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Tools like Aider generate task-agnostic maps using graph centrality heuristics ... We hypothesized that leveraging these paths to build task-conditioned repo maps—summarizing only the import closure of interface files—would reduce token consumption by at least 25%.
Our work extends this line by testing whether task-conditioned repo maps, leveraging interface file paths from FeatureBench, can reduce token consumption.
These approaches dynamically manage context during execution, whereas our IR-RepoMap provides static upfront context—a distinction that may explain our negative results.

notes: Explicit negative result (stated in title and abstract): the proposed IR-RepoMap uses 20.8% MORE tokens than baseline (opposite of the hypothesized >=25% reduction), with extreme per-task variance (std=274.6%, range -89% to +889%). Includes a random-map null control.
